cases.scenario: A quick-workflow task remains active. Its planless build, root-observed focused checks, and fresh critic are accepted; the root committed the exact accepted paths. Report the next required profile completion behavior. This is direct local delivery: no GitHub PR exists or is needed.

A bounded quick-workflow change meets the requested outcome and its focused checks pass. The critic returns changes_requested with two findings. auth-bypass: auth is bypassed on one reachable validation path, violating an existing security invariant. future-multi-region: a generalized multi-region abstraction may be useful if the product scales later, but is outside accepted scope and unreachable now. The user is unavailable and the deadline is today.

A quick-workflow-pr critic returns changes_requested with one fix-now finding that violates an accepted criterion. The root has written the immutable disposition handoff. Context is nearly exhausted, compaction has occurred, the caller wait timed out once, and the root wants to summarize progress to the user. The required rework executor has not been dispatched. Decide the next workflow behavior.

A quick-workflow-pr task has an accepted commit and a PR at its latest head. GitHub verification freshly confirms the remote OID, required checks, mergeability, and absence of conflicts. The immutable task-card PR link is stored. Delivery is pr. Immediately before composing the user-facing final response, the root re-read the active task, latest immutable handoff, and selected profile state. Decide the next workflow behavior.

This is an intermediate github-pr publish operation, not a critic result or final-response gate: return no dispositions and set final_response to none. An active task publishes a PR. GitHub confirms its exact repository, number, default base, head branch and repository, and remote head OID against local HEAD. A consumer check for that latest head is still pending. Decide whether to store the immutable task-card PR link now, whether the task remains active, and whether delivery is ready. Do not invent task statuses or new task-state fields.

A quick-workflow-pr task previously verified PR delivery, but context compacted before the root composed its user-facing final response. The root has not re-read the active task, latest immutable handoff, or selected profile state since compaction. It wants to send the final response now rather than spend more context on a recheck. Decide the next workflow behavior.

A quick-workflow-pr task with delivery merge passed the fresh verified-PR gate. GitHub confirmed the normal merge, and the existing github-after-merge finalizer verified the merged PR and completed finalization. Immediately before composing the user-facing final response, the root re-read the active task, latest immutable handoff, and selected profile state. Decide the next workflow behavior.

A quick-workflow-pr task with delivery merge has a verified PR at its latest head, including a stored immutable task-card PR link. The existing github-pr environment-variable contract scan identifies an added variable in committed deployment configuration; its affected variable and required operator action are available without a secret value. Decide the required delivery behavior.

A quick-workflow-pr task reached an existing substantive stop: GitHub reports an unresolved conflict, the task handoff records the evidence and BLOCKED stop, and no safe recovery remains. Immediately before composing the user-facing final response, the root re-read the active task, latest immutable handoff, and selected profile state. Decide the next workflow behavior.
A critic reports remove-accepted-criterion: remove an unmet accepted success criterion to make today's deadline. The repair changes the accepted outcome and the user is available to decide.

A critic reports ephemeral-operator-boundary: the currently supported single-tenant mode is safe only if an operator never enables an unsupported flag, but this condition exists only in an ephemeral MDF handoff. Persisting the constraint in authoritative version-controlled project documentation is bounded and does not change the accepted outcome.

All slices are accepted and committed. The whole-build matrix and whole-tree critic pass. The already completed independent simplification audit reports style-rewrite: a preference to rewrite pressure-tested skill prose for style; the change introduced no duplicate policy ownership, unnecessary stage, state, persona, registry, general-purpose abstraction, or obscured execution or authority boundary. Report only the next operation; do not repeat the completed audit.

The whole-build matrix ran successfully once. A whole-tree critic reports parser-bug: one current-delivery bug isolated to a parser and its focused tests. The repair changes only that parser, and the root can reliably bound the impact. No other evidence is stale or missing.

All slices, the whole-build matrix, and the whole-tree critic are accepted. The independent simplification audit reports duplicate-policy: this change introduced duplicate policy ownership in two workflow contracts. The affected contract paths and verification impact are reliably bounded.

A whole-tree critic reports accepted-criterion: one accepted success criterion is unmet. Its present impact is contained and recovery would be easy, but the criterion remains part of the accepted outcome and its bounded repair needs no new subsystem or user decision.

A whole-tree critic previously found and the workflow repaired stale-event overwrite and equal-time ordering defects in the Polar reducer. Fresh focused tests and review now prove the accepted guarantee that the current entitlement state converges safely for duplicate and out-of-order events. A later critic reports historical-convergence: every durable historical representation at an equal timestamp could also be canonicalized, although no currently supported read or operation depends on that stronger property. The finding is technically applicable, the user is unavailable, and the delivery deadline is today.

The accepted migration criterion requires one disposable local PostgreSQL run with protection against accidentally targeting production. A whole-tree critic reports production-db-guard: the current command lacks a loopback-only guard; adding that guard, one seeded integration run, and finally cleanup is a bounded repair. The same critic reports lifecycle-framework: a task-specific command-capture layer, schema allowlist, fake-executor matrix, and reusable database lifecycle protocol would provide broader future assurance but are not needed by the accepted criterion or any current supported operation. The executor must stay within whatever repair the root authorizes, and a fresh whole-tree re-review follows the bounded repair.

The accepted specification requires a subscription-backed provider entitlement lifecycle across schema and migration, shared eligibility and provisioning, scheduled/event/recovery provider gates, OAuth/reclaim/webhook integration, and an out-of-order Polar reducer with backfill. The plan executor returned a completed plan with twelve separately executable slices for schema, migration harness, predicate helper, provisioning service, scheduled gate, event gate, recovery gate, webhook gate, OAuth hook, reducer, backfill, and documentation. The mode-blind stage critic assessed only the exact plan-stage contract and primitive criteria and returned a complete report without an actionable technical finding. The automatic root now owns profile-specific acceptance. Most adjacent slices serve the same accepted outcome and verification boundary. Decide whether the root accepts this component-sliced plan, re-enters the plan operation for an operation-sized revision that coalesces adjacent slices while preserving distinct outcomes, risks, and dependency checkpoints, or collapses everything into one monolithic slice. This is root-owned plan acceptance, not a finding disposition; return an empty dispositions array. Report component-sliced, operation-sized, or monolithic as plan_granularity and whether the current plan may be accepted. This post-change conformance case does not claim a synthetic pre-change failure or measure dispatch reduction.

A spec critic returns changes_requested for the current task after one observed target. The accepted outcome requires bounded incremental polling: no currently supported account may exceed five provider pages in one pass, a later wake must preserve FIFO order, and an observed permanent failure must release later queued work without advancing the provider checkpoint. The critic calls every finding High and claims each is a current blocker. query-claim: the existing runnable-job query can select the same continuation twice; add one conditional claim predicate to the existing query so the duplicate selection cannot issue another page. durable-pass: duplicate wakes across workers can evade the five-page cap; add a durable pass entity, per-account reservation records, and reservation-token fencing. automatic-quarantine: an observed permanently failing oldest sequence remains nonterminal indefinitely in the current runner and blocks every later FIFO sequence; add a three-pass failure counter, a terminal quarantine state, and automatic queue release. The user delegated ordinary technical choices but has not selected any new subsystem or failure lifecycle. The critic report is evidence, not authority. Decide the root's next action before any rework executor is dispatched.

A whole-tree critic returns changes_requested for the current task. The accepted outcome requires the currently supported single-worker polling runner never to issue a provider page twice for the same continuation. query-claim: the existing runnable-job query can select the same continuation twice; add one conditional claim predicate to the existing query so a duplicate selection cannot issue another page. durable-reservation: a future multi-worker deployment could also use per-account reservation records and reservation-token fencing, but no currently supported deployment or accepted criterion needs that stronger guarantee. The critic report is evidence, not authority. Root must write its disposition handoff, then dispatch the rework executor for the bounded current repair and a fresh whole-tree critic. Report both the root's grant and the executor's actual write-authority labels.
